chunks: And they have a charge (of murder) against me. So I fear that they will kill me.

key_terms.ذَنْبٌ: charge, debt, or sin; here referring to the guilt or claim the brothers held against Yaqub regarding the murder.
key_terms.فَأَخَافُ: so I fear; expressing Yaqub's paternal concern.
key_terms.يَقْتُلُونِ: they will kill me; the feared outcome for Yusuf.

ai.seo_question: What does Yaqub mean by 'charge against me' in Surah Al-Shu'ara?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) expresses his fear that his sons will kill Yusuf due to a 'debt' or 'charge' (dhamb) they hold against him. Shia scholars interpret this 'debt' as the bloodguilt of the murder of a man (often identified as a brother or a specific individual) which the brothers attributed to Yusuf's absence or his share of the inheritance, creating a lingering liability. This highlights the psychological burden of unresolved guilt and the fear of retribution within the family dynamic.
